page: Amazon Web Services d3en.12xlarge is a dense storage instance optimized for network and EBS performance. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key feature of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, which consists of 335,520 GB of local HDD storage. Additionally, it features a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps and runs on the Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier, as does single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores reach average levels. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register in the middle 50% tier. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput consistently perform at average levels. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference speeds for small and medium models are average, though prompt processing for large 70B models drops to the bottom 25% tier.

The d3en.12xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive storage capacity and high network throughput without the premium cost of solid-state drives. The primary trade-off is the reliance on local HDD storage instead of NVMe SSDs, which limits random I/O performance despite the massive 335.52 TB capacity. The instance is highly suited for storage-heavy workloads such as data lakes, massive data warehousing, distributed file systems, and large-scale log processing where sequential read/write throughput and high network bandwidth are prioritized over low-latency random storage access.
